section_7_composition_feature_preparatio.qualifier_distribution_and_treatment: resolve_composition_column's DEFAULT resolver preserves the genuine numeric value regardless of qualifier (trace/balance/range/exact/None) -- qualifiers are NOT used to null a numeric value by default; a caller could opt into qualifier-based nulling via a custom qualifier_strategy, but no such custom strategy is used anywhere in this project's frozen pipeline. Verified in Notebook 02: the library default was found already correct for this dataset -- no custom qualifier strategy was needed.
section_7_composition_feature_preparatio.missing_value_treatment: SimpleImputer(strategy='median', add_indicator=True, keep_empty_features=True), fit per-fold inside the CV pipeline (never on the full dataset before splitting)
section_7_composition_feature_preparatio.missing_indicator_treatment: add_indicator=True on the numeric imputer -- a binary 'was this feature missing' column is added per numeric feature, so missingness itself is available as signal without imputation silently hiding it
section_7_composition_feature_preparatio.scaling_policy: StandardScaler applied only for scale-sensitive models (ridge, svr) via modelling_lib.MODELS_REQUIRING_SCALING; tree ensembles (random_forest, gradient_boosting) and the dummy baseline are never scaled
section_7_composition_feature_preparatio.processing_key_exclusion_reason: processing_key was investigated in Notebook 02 and found to be a near-unique per-paper identifier for the large majority of its values (22/26 distinct values traced to a single DOI each) -- using it as a feature would let a model learn 'which paper this row came from' (a DOI-fingerprinting leak) rather than a genuine physical processing feature, so it was excluded as a predictor before any model was run.
section_7_composition_feature_preparatio.processing_test_status_not_used_as_predi: processing_identity_status and test_conditions_status are used ONLY to group/stratify already-fixed OOF prediction errors for the RQ4 diagnostic (Section 11) -- they are never passed as columns into build_preprocessor/build_model_pipeline anywhere in modelling_lib.py or any of the six notebooks. This was a design decision made in the Notebook 02 planning discussion, before any model was run, not a post-hoc restriction.
section_7_composition_feature_preparatio.feature_and_cohort_decisions_predate_mod: Notebook 02 (feature selection: coverage thresholds, qualifier check, processing_key investigation) was completed and its TARGET_CONFIGS frozen in modelling_lib.py BEFORE Notebook 03 (the first model run) was written. The selection_rule thresholds (>=20 observations AND >=5 DOI) were fixed as library constants (DEFAULT_MIN_OBSERVATIONS_FOR_FEATURE, DEFAULT_MIN_DOI_FOR_FEATURE) before any model saw the data.

section_8_final_modelling_design.corrected_uts_handling: UTS_MPa_corrected = raw UTS_MPa, with the single confirmed GPa->MPa row multiplied by 1000; a manual_unit_correction_applied boolean flag records which row was corrected. The raw UTS_MPa column is never mutated. apply_known_data_corrections() raises ValueError if the expected raw value at the correction key no longer matches, guarding against silently mis-applying a stale correction.

model_configurations.ridge: sklearn.linear_model.Ridge(alpha=1.0), random_state threaded through for API uniformity (Ridge is deterministic for the solver used)
model_configurations.svr: sklearn.svm.SVR() with library defaults (no random_state parameter exists on SVR)
model_configurations.dummy_mean: sklearn.dummy.DummyRegressor(strategy='mean') -- reference baseline, deliberately kept OUT of MODEL_FACTORIES (the 4-model research set) via a separate BASELINE_MODEL_FACTORIES registry

section_8_final_modelling_design.random_seeds: DEFAULT_RANDOM_STATE = 42, used for every stochastic model (RF, GB) and threaded through Ridge/dummy for API uniformity; GroupKFold itself has no shuffling/random_state parameter
section_8_final_modelling_design.cross_validation: GroupKFold, min_splits=max_splits=5 (fixed at 5-fold for all three targets -- an earlier 8-fold run for UTS/YS was a procedural error, corrected before any result was reported)
section_8_final_modelling_design.imputation: SimpleImputer(strategy='median', add_indicator=True, keep_empty_features=True), fit fold-by-fold inside each training split only -- median is computed from that fold's training data, never leaking test-fold information
section_8_final_modelling_design.scaling: StandardScaler for ridge/svr only (MODELS_REQUIRING_SCALING); none for random_forest/gradient_boosting/dummy_mean
section_8_final_modelling_design.identical_doi_fold_assignment_across_mod: ONE GroupKFold cv object is built per target and reused across all 5 models (run_target_experiment) -- GroupKFold has no shuffling, so identical groups always produce identical splits, and building the cv object once (not once per model) GUARANTEES this rather than merely making it likely. Explicitly verified in Notebook 03 via an exact (fold, sorted DOI-set) comparison across all 5 models for all 3 targets -- printed result: True for every target.
section_8_final_modelling_design.held_out_doi_never_in_training_fold: GroupKFold partitions by the group column (doi): every observation belonging to a DOI assigned to a fold's test split is guaranteed absent from that fold's training split, by construction of sklearn's GroupKFold -- no two folds share any DOI.
section_8_final_modelling_design.oof_prediction_construction: cross_validate_model runs the CV loop manually (not cross_val_score) so each fold's held-out predict() call populates one row of oof_predictions per test observation; concatenated across all folds, this covers every observation in the cohort exactly once.

RQ4.wording: Does prediction error differ according to the completeness of composition, processing and testing information?
RQ4.observed_result: Across all three targets and all three contextual dimensions (processing identity, test-information resolution, composition completeness), Random Forest OOF MAE does not show a consistent, well-supported pattern relative to the dummy-mean reference. Composition completeness is monotonically decreasing with error only for elongation (low=10.1, medium=7.9, high=2.9), not for UTS or YS. Gradient Boosting agrees with Random Forest on the lower-error group in all 9 dimension-target comparisons (100%).
RQ4.bounded_interpretation: No consistent relationship was identified between contextual-information completeness and prediction error.
RQ4.limitation: Most subgroup comparisons rest on exploratory (5-9 DOI) or very_limited (<5 DOI) support; only 3 of 9 dimension-target comparisons reach supported_descriptive (>=10 DOI). The counter-intuitive processing-status pattern (confirmed_baseline showing lower error than confirmed_explicit for UTS/YS) is confounded with the dummy reference showing the identical tendency -- i.e. confirmed_baseline is likely an easier subgroup, not evidence of a completeness effect. This is an observational error comparison, not a causal test, and not a processing/test-feature ablation (neither field was ever used as a model predictor).
